  Line or code reference: 226
  Problem: The `cross_ref_prs` call uses bare `gh api` (no retry wrapper), while plan.yml's equivalent `CROSS_REF_PRS` call at plan.yml:578 uses `gh_retry`. A transient API failure on `gh api` is swallowed by `|| true`, setting `cross_ref_prs=""`, which silently passes the PR-exists check and allows a duplicate implementation run. This is a pre-existing asymmetry the original step also had (bare `gh api`), so the PR does not introduce it, but it weakens the new mention-only guard in the implement path.
  Why it fails at runtime: Transient network error during timeline fetch yields empty cross_ref_prs, head_branch_prs still runs and may find the conventional-head PR, but a closing-keyword-only PR on the timeline is missed.

The new alias fallback returns a non-empty string for `Target branch:` lines when `Integration branch:` is absent. No backward compatibility break, but the semantic shift is worth noting: a body without `Integration branch:` now resolves where it previously returned `""`.
  Why it fails at runtime: N/A — callers gate on `if child_branch:` / `if not tracking_branch:`, which correctly handles both empty string and new non-empty alias values.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 222-238 (closing_kw_re + jq test()), `cross_ref_prs` capture at line 226 (`|| true`)
  Problem: `cross_ref_prs="$(gh api --paginate "..." --jq '...' || true)"`. When the timeline call succeeds but emits a `null` body for a cross-referenced PR, the jq filter `((.body // "") | test(...; "i"))` falls back to `""` and `test("", "i")` returns `false`. So a real implementation PR whose body is missing/null is silently reclassified as `mention`, and the gate does NOT skip.
  Why it fails at runtime: The pre-existing gate at line 261 reads `[ -s "${PR_EXISTS_FILE}" ]` to decide. If the implementation PR has an empty body in the timeline event, the gate falls through, executes implement, and only GitHub's `gh pr create --head` rejection catches it. The plan.yml gate has the same shape (lines 595-603), with the additional consequence that planning is silently re-run instead of skipped.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
- .github/workflows/plan.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 591-593, `HEAD_BRANCH_PRS="$(gh_retry gh api --paginate "repos/${repo_slug}/pulls?state=open&head=${repo_owner}:${impl_head}" ... )"`
  Problem: Unlike `cross_ref_prs` in implement.yml which is captured under `|| true`, the `HEAD_BRANCH_PRS` capture in plan.yml has no `|| true`. Under `set -euo pipefail`, a 5xx or rate-limit response from `gh_retry` (after its retries are exhausted) makes the command exit non-zero.
  Why it fails at runtime: `gh_retry`'s 4xx responses, such as 404 for a deleted issue, do not trigger retries and also fail the step. This is documented as intended and consistent with the pre-existing timeline call, but it remains an asymmetry.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
  SEVERITY: NIT
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py
  Line or code reference: lines 46-63 (INTEGRATION_BRANCH_LINE_RE and TARGET_BRANCH_LINE_RE both declared at module scope)
  Problem: `extract_integration_branch` accepts both `Integration branch:` and `Target branch:` in any issue body. This is a behavior expansion for issues that historically relied on the strict `Integration branch:` parser.
  Why it fails at runtime: A non-orchestrator issue with `Target branch:` text in its body may now route to the named branch instead of the default branch. This is the documented intent, and canonical `Integration branch:` behavior remains unchanged.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
  SEVERITY: NIT

- changelog.d/4075-plan-gate-mention-only-prs.md
  Line or code reference: line 9, "What this means for operators" paragraph — "A `Target branch:` that names a branch that does not exist fails the resolver the same way a missing `Integration branch:` does, and the workflow falls back to the default branch with a warning."
  Problem: Internally contradictory and contradicts the shipped behavior. `scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh` `resolve_ref()` (lines 76-82, 98-101) returns 1 with an `::error::` when the declared branch is missing — that is exactly what the new fixture `tests/fixtures/integration_ref_resolver/child_target_branch_alias_missing_fails.json` pins (`expected_exit_code: 1`), and README §12a (line 1500 of the diff) says the pipeline "fails safe instead of silently falling back to default branch".
  Why it fails at runtime: Not a runtime failure, but the changelog fragment is user-facing release documentation (`scripts/assemble_changelog.py` folds it verbatim into CHANGELOG.md), and the sentence misinforms operators about the failure mode.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- .github/workflows/plan.yml (lines 588-601 of the diff) and .github/workflows/implement.yml (lines 240-256 of the diff)
  Line or code reference: the `pulls?state=open&head=${repo_owner}:${impl_head}` lookup plus the closing-keyword `test(...)` classification
  Problem: The new gates recognize only two shapes of "the issue's own PR": head branch exactly `ai/issue-<N>`, or a body closing keyword. A PR that GitHub will auto-close on merge via the "Linked issues" sidebar UI, with no `Closes #N` keyword in the body, on any other branch is no longer detected.
  Why it fails at runtime: A human opens `Fix the widget` on branch `hotfix/widget`, links issue #4073 via the sidebar UI, and the timeline emits `cross-referenced`; the body lacks a closing keyword; the head is not `ai/issue-4073`; the gate reports zero implementation PRs and plans/implements a duplicate.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
